title: The rate limiter keys on an unvalidated client-supplied `X-Forwarded-For`, so every public endpoint's limit is bypassed by rotating one header
claimUnderTest: src/api/rate_limit.py:9-11 — "60 requests/minute per IP … 1000 requests/hour per IP (burst cap)", and server.py:2840-2842 "Also applies rate limiting to public endpoints … to protect against scraper abuse."
observed: `_client_ip_from_request` returns the FIRST comma-separated entry of `X-Forwarded-For` whenever the header is present, with no trusted-proxy check and no fallback preference for `request.client.host`. nginx sets `X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for`, which APPENDS `$remote_addr` to whatever the client sent — so in production the first entry is entirely attacker-controlled. Measured on a second backend booted without `RATE_LIMIT_BYPASS_IPS`: the real client IP was driven to a hard 429, and 20 consecutive requests sent from that same socket with rotating `X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.N` all returned 200.

reproduction.command:
# boot a backend on :8001 without RATE_LIMIT_BYPASS_IPS, then:
for i in $(seq 1 70); do curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/health; done
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/health   # 429
for i in $(seq 1 20); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%s ' -H "X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.$i" http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/health; done
reproduction.expected: 429 for all 20, because they originate from the throttled socket

numericProof.formula: 429_count over 20 spoofed-XFF requests issued from an already-throttled socket

userImpact: The scraper-abuse defence the module exists for does not exist. Anyone can pull the 2.08 MB `/api/public/league` contract, or the 47 KB `/api/news` feed, at whatever rate the box will serve — and, because `/api/auth/login` sits behind the same limiter, the login endpoint has no effective throttle either (W22-F003).

priorFinding.note: No prior finding mentions X-Forwarded-For or the rate limiter.

whatWorks: The token-bucket arithmetic itself is correct and thread-safe: 60 requests pass and the 61st gets 429 with a sane `Retry-After`, refill is proportional to elapsed time, and the `_MAX_TRACKED_IPS` eviction bounds memory. The limiter fails open around a raising `should_rate_limit`, which is the right posture. Nothing here is wrong except the key.
rootCause: `_client_ip_from_request` trusts a hop-by-hop header unconditionally. The comment "First entry in the chain is the original client" is true only when every hop appends and the leftmost hop is itself trusted — which is exactly what `$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for` does NOT guarantee for a directly-reachable client.
requiredRepair: Prefer `X-Real-IP` (nginx sets it from `$remote_addr` and OVERWRITES, so it is not client-controlled) and fall back to `request.client.host`; use `X-Forwarded-For` only after stripping a configured count of trusted proxy hops from the RIGHT. `_MAX_TRACKED_IPS`-based eviction also becomes a memory-exhaustion lever while the key is attacker-chosen.
dependencies: nginx already sets `X-Real-IP $remote_addr` in both `location /api/` and `location /`, so no deploy change is needed.
